transcript.t: Michael Faraday was born in 1791 into a poor family in England. He left school at a young age, and at fourteen he started to work for a bookbinder.
In his free time, he read the books he was binding and learned a lot about science. Later he went to lectures by a famous chemist, wrote down his notes carefully and sent them to him.
The chemist liked the notes and gave Faraday a job as an assistant. Faraday worked very hard and made important discoveries about electricity.
Today we use electricity every day, so we should remember him.
